GLST 101.description: Introduction to global problems presented from different disciplinary perspectives with emphasis on the challenges of globalization, including poverty, trade and development, environmental change, peace and conflict, migration, and intercultural relations.
GLST 101.subject: GLST
GLST 101.title: Global Studies: Context, Connection, and Change

GLST 107.description: Interdisciplinary analysis of global affairs using quantitative approaches to development, global governance, and transnational policy issues.
GLST 107.subject: GLST
GLST 107.title: Global Economic Relations

GLST 140.description: Survey of the Middle East’s historical, cultural, religious, and social diversity, emphasizing regional dynamics and global interconnections through interdisciplinary study.
GLST 140.subject: GLST
GLST 140.title: Introduction to Middle East Studies

GLST 201.description: Interdisciplinary exploration of how people, movements, and institutions shape global change.
GLST 201.subject: GLST
GLST 201.title: Diplomacy, Advocacy, and Global Policy

GLST 220.description: Given that literature represents real policies and practices in the contemporary world and our ethical responsibility as global citizens, the course will focus on literature from different periods, nations, and regions across the world in order to better understand the way human experiences and different cultures relate. All literature will be read and taught in English.
GLST 220.subject: GLST
GLST 220.title: Introduction to Global Studies Through Literature

GLST 300.description: Critical, historical, and theoretical introduction to modern development practice. Includes extended discussions of contemporary best practices in the field.
GLST 300.subject: GLST
GLST 300.title: Introduction to International Development

GLST 305.description: Global patterns and processes of migration through multi-disciplinary perspectives, addressing the types, causes, and effects of migration. Possible topics include labor migration, refugees and asylum, climate migration, migration controls, and processes of inclusion and exclusion.
GLST 305.subject: GLST
GLST 305.title: Global Migration

GLST 308.description: Provides the foundation for the study of globalized film and media industries.
GLST 308.subject: GLST
GLST 308.title: Global Media Industries

GLST 320.description: Investigation of human-environment interactions and their effects on global population health and health disparities through the lens of Health and Medical geography.
GLST 320.subject: GLST
GLST 320.title: Global Health Geographies

GLST 350.description: Examination of the institutional design, operational missions, and decision-making processes of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization and its role in global affairs.
GLST 350.subject: GLST
GLST 350.title: NATO in Global Affairs

GLST 369.description: History of capitalist economic behavior and culture in various premodern societies: the Ancient Middle East, Classical Greece, the Roman Empire, early Islamic society, medieval Christian and Islamic states, the Mongol period and the era of global expansionism; evaluation of competing theories about premodern economic life and the meaning of capitalism
GLST 369.subject: GLST
GLST 369.title: History of Capitalism 1: Ancient and Medieval World

GLST 370.description: A history of capitalism and its evolving definitions in Europe from the Middle Ages to the 20th Century, including its role in agriculture, mechanical industry, international trade, and colonialism and domination.
GLST 370.subject: GLST
GLST 370.title: History of Capitalism 2: From the Industrial Revolution to the Global Economy

GLST 378.description: An introduction to traditional and popular music styles from several cultures and regions in Africa as well as the African diaspora.
GLST 378.subject: GLST
GLST 378.title: Music of the African World

GLST 380.description: Geopolitical, historical, cultural, and economic geographies of human rights around the world; issues of development, environment, health, inequality, violence.
GLST 380.subject: GLST
GLST 380.title: Global Human Rights

GLST 391.description: Selected topics in Global Studies. May be repeated with a change in topic. May be taken three times for credit.
GLST 391.subject: GLST
GLST 391.title: Topics in Global Studies

GLST 401.description: Special topics seminar focused on integrating interdisciplinary concepts and understandings necessary for living, working, and thinking in a globally interdependent world.
GLST 401.subject: GLST
GLST 401.title: Global Studies Capstone

GLST 490.description: Academic counterpart to a professional work experience in which global or international affairs play a central role. Provides an introduction to foreign affairs and intercultural interactions in a working environment. Introduction to career possibilities for a student trained in global studies. Global Studies major with 3.0 or better GPA and completion of at least 45 credits.
GLST 490.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: Two courses from the following: ANTH 102; GEOG 121; GEOG 210; LING 101; POLI 101; RELG 101.
GLST 490.subject: GLST
GLST 490.title: Global Studies Internship

GLST 531.description: Intensive study of global-level issues from a variety of disciplinary perspectives.
GLST 531.subject: GLST
GLST 531.title: Advanced Topics in Global Studies
